subproblem.title: Unit orientations: operator-norm bound and the interior product ξ⌞ν orienting Q ∩ ν^⊥ (Simon Ch. 6, 4.3)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Write Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k for the continuous alternating k-forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖, and MultiVector P k := (Λ^k →L[ℝ] ℝ). Call ξ ∈ MultiVector P k a unit orientation of a linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P (contract IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q) if there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_k) in ℝ^P with span τ = Q such that ξ(α) = α(τ) for every α ∈ Λ^k, or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every α ∈ Λ^k. (a) If ξ ∈ MultiVector P n is a unit orientation of Q, then |ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every α ∈ Λ^n. (b) Let ξ ∈ MultiVector P (n+1) be a unit orientation of Q, let v ∈ Q with v ≠ 0, put ν := |v|⁻¹v, and let ζ ∈ MultiVector P n satisfy ζ(α) = ξ(ν♭ ∧ α) for every α ∈ Λ^n, where ν♭ := ⟨ν, ·⟩ (innerSL ℝ ν) and ν♭ ∧ α := alternatizeUncurryFin(ν♭.smulRight α), i.e. (ν♭ ∧ α)(w_0, …, w_n) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, w_i⟩ α(w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_n). Then ζ is a unit orientation of Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥ = Q ∩ v^⊥. This is Simon's claim in 4.3 that ξ⌞ν, defined by ⟨ξ⌞ν, α⟩ = ⟨ξ, ν ∧ α⟩, is a unit simple n-vector orienting T_xM ∩ ν^⊥ when ξ orients T_xM and ν ∈ T_xM is a unit vector.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ α| ≤ ‖α‖) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P (n + 1)) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (v : Euclid P) (ζ : MultiVector P n), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → v ∈ Q → v ≠ 0 → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ζ α = ξ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ (‖v‖⁻¹ • v)).smulRight α))) → IsUnitOrientationOf ζ (Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ v)ᗮ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the supplied proof of the parent node slice_family, steps 0(a), 3(a) and 3(c). Simon Ch. 6, 4.3 (book/chapter-06.txt ll. 1208–1218, printed p. 155) states the conclusion of (b) without proof ("is simple ∈ Λ_{n−1}(T_xM_t) ⊂ Λ_{n−1}(T_xM) and has unit length", with ⟨v⌞w, a⟩ = ⟨v, w ∧ a⟩). The argument below is the one written out in the supplied proof, with the details filled in. For a family w = (w_1, …, w_k) of vectors, α(w) denotes the value of the k-covector α at w.

Part (a).
1. By the definition of IsUnitOrientationOf there is τ : Fin n → ℝ^P, orthonormal, with span τ = Q, and either ξ(α) = α(τ) for all α ∈ Λ^n or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for all α ∈ Λ^n. In both cases |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)|.
2. By the operator-norm inequality for continuous alternating maps (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ · ∏_{i} |τ_i|.
3. Each |τ_i| = 1 because τ is orthonormal, so the product equals 1 (it is the empty product 1 when n = 0). Hence |ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every α ∈ Λ^n.

Part (b).
4. Dimension of Q. By the definition of IsUnitOrientationOf there are τ : Fin (n+1) → ℝ^P, orthonormal, with span τ = Q, and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(β) = s·β(τ) for every β ∈ Λ^{n+1}. An orthonormal family is linearly independent, so τ is a basis of Q and dim Q = n + 1. In particular τ is an orthonormal basis of Q.
5. The unit vector ν. Since v ≠ 0, |v| > 0 and ν := |v|⁻¹v satisfies |ν| = 1. Since Q is a subspace and v ∈ Q, ν ∈ Q. Moreover span{ν} = span{v} (ν is a nonzero multiple of v), so v^⊥ = ν^⊥.
6. Dimension of Q'. Put Q' := Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥. Since span{v} ⊆ Q, Q is the orthogonal direct sum of span{v} and Q', so dim span{v} + dim Q' = dim Q (Mathlib Submodule.finrank_add_inf_finrank_orthogonal). As dim span{v} = 1, dim Q' = n.
7. Choose an orthonormal basis τ' = (τ'_1, …, τ'_n) of Q', indexed by Fin n. For instance, take stdOrthonormalBasis of Q' and reindex it along dim Q' = n with finCongr. Orthonormality transfers to ℝ^P along the isometric inclusion (Q'.subtypeₗᵢ.orthonormal_comp_iff). Viewed in ℝ^P, τ' is orthonormal, span τ' = Q', each τ'_j ∈ Q, and ⟨ν, τ'_j⟩ = 0 because τ'_j ⊥ v and ν is a multiple of v.
8. The basis σ. Let σ := (ν, τ'_1, …, τ'_n) = Fin.cons ν τ' : Fin (n+1) → ℝ^P. It is orthonormal (|ν| = 1, τ' orthonormal, ⟨ν, τ'_j⟩ = 0), all its vectors lie in Q, and it has n + 1 = dim Q vectors. Being linearly independent, σ is an orthonormal basis of Q. (In Lean: OrthonormalBasis.mk, with ⊤ ≤ span obtained from basisOfOrthonormalOfCardEqFinrank; evaluate its vectors with OrthonormalBasis.coe_mk.)
9. Uniform sign. Let β ∈ Λ^{n+1}. Its restriction β_Q to Q is β composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot (β.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap Q.subtype). It is an alternating (n+1)-form on the (n+1)-dimensional space Q. Hence β_Q = β_Q(σ) · det_σ, where det_σ is the determinant with respect to the basis σ (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at the basis τ of Q gives β(τ) = det_σ(τ) · β(σ). Since σ and τ are orthonormal bases of the same real inner product space Q, det_σ(τ) ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Put ε := s · det_σ(τ) ∈ {1, −1}. It does not depend on β, and ξ(β) = s·β(τ) = ε·β(σ) for every β ∈ Λ^{n+1}.
10. Expansion of the wedge. Let α ∈ Λ^n. By the formula for alternatizeUncurryFin (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply), (ν♭ ∧ α)(σ) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ α(σ_0, …, σ̂_i, …, σ_n), where the hat means omission (Fin.removeNth). For i = 0 the term is ⟨ν, ν⟩ α(τ') = α(τ'), because |ν| = 1 and removing the 0-th entry of Fin.cons ν τ' leaves τ'. For 1 ≤ i ≤ n, σ_i = τ'_i and ⟨ν, τ'_i⟩ = 0, so the term vanishes. Hence (ν♭ ∧ α)(σ) = α(τ').
11. Consequently, for every α ∈ Λ^n, ζ(α) = ξ(ν♭ ∧ α) = ε·(ν♭ ∧ α)(σ) = ε·α(τ'). This uses the hypothesis on ζ, step 9 with β := ν♭ ∧ α, and step 10.
12. Conclusion. τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P is orthonormal with span τ' = Q' = Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥. Either ζ(α) = α(τ') for all α (if ε = 1) or ζ(α) = −α(τ') for all α (if ε = −1). This is exactly IsUnitOrientationOf ζ (Q ⊓ (span{v})^⊥). When n = 0 the same argument applies: τ' is the empty family, Q' = 0 = span ∅, σ = (ν), and α(τ') is the value of the 0-covector α. ∎
proof_key_steps: (b) dim Q = n+1. ν := |v|⁻¹v ∈ Q is a unit vector, and Q' := Q ⊓ span{v}^⊥ has dimension n. Take an orthonormal basis τ' of Q'; then σ := Fin.cons ν τ' is an orthonormal basis of Q.
Uniform sign: on Q, β = β(σ)·det_σ (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det) and det_σ(τ) = ±1 for orthonormal bases, so ξ(β) = εβ(σ) for one ε ∈ {±1}.
Hence ζ(α) = εα(τ') for all α, i.e. ζ is a unit orientation of Q ⊓ span{v}^⊥.

audit.reason: The prose and type agree. Orthonormal evaluation proves the operator-norm bound; the orthogonal decomposition, uniform determinant sign and explicit wedge expansion prove the interior-product orientation, including n = 0. No circular reliance occurs.
